newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander confirms June 9 share split.
newsitem.headline: Santander confirms June 9 share split.

text.p: Spain's leading bank Santander confirmed on Tuesday its share split, which will reduce the nominal value to 250 pesetas from 750 pesetas, will take place on June 9.
On July 31, the group will pay its first interim dividend of 27 pesetas gross per new 250 peseta nominal share, a 15.7 percent rise compared with last year's interim dividend.
In the note accompanying the results, the bank said its rate of non-performing loans had dropped to 3.1 percent.
"The rate of non-performing loans of the bank in Spain is 1.08 percent. Abroad, the rate is 3.97 percent and overall it is 3.1 percent," Jose Tejon, bank comptroller, told reporters.
Executive Vice President Francisco Luzon added that "growth at the bank is focused on value-added services."
Santander noted that the first quarter results do not include the sale of stakes in Airtel and British Telecommunications.
"The sale agreement has been signed to be executed in December or before, if the buyer so wishes," Tejon said.
The results also exclude the acquisitions of Banco Mexicano, Banco Comercial Antioqueno and Banco Geral do Comercio in Brazil, which had not been completed at the end of the first quarter.
